WHAT I READ: AGENTS.md; docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md; docs/infra/managent/spec.md §managent standing; the T294 brief; src/managent/main.zig (standing section); src/claimlint.zig (C7 section, checkFindings, parseFindingsFile, parseRegister); tools/hooks/pre-commit (the summary-reading doctrine); tools/regression-managent-resume.sh (control-script pattern); docs/infra/dispatch/STANDING-CONSOLIDATE.md (brief template); findings/README.md + findings-schema.json.

WHAT I DID: (1) Added STANDING-ABSORB to standing_templates with threshold constant ABSORB_C7_THRESHOLD=5 and full rationale (0 = permanently-red-gate failure; 1-4 = in-flight noise band; 5 = session-sized, fires with margin on the smallest observed genuine backlog of 10). (2) C7 is parsed from the SAME claimlint run the C3 trigger uses, from the summary line 'C7 unabsorbed findings: N' (leading digits, immune to the '(FAILS)' suffix) — never reimplemented. (3) Per-file composition aggregated from claimlint's own 'UNABSORBED ... in <file>' detail lines, printed as 'per file:' (sorted). (4) Trigger is ABSOLUTE (count > 5), not change-based. (5) New brief docs/infra/dispatch/STANDING-ABSORB.md; spec.md updated to five triggers. (6) tools/regression-managent-standing.sh wired into zig build test — the standing mechanism previously had NO controls at all, which the brief told me to state. Controls: null (empty findings → C7=0, explicit 'at/below threshold, no trigger', nothing registered) and seeded (6 synthetic unabsorbed claims → C7=6 > 5, trigger fires, names the count, registers dispatchable STANDING-ABSORB in the scratch kanban, per-file 'T294SEED-absorb.json: 6'). Both PASS in /tmp/weizigo scratch repos; live kanban/findings/CLAIMS.md untouched.

WHAT I FOUND (all verified): (a) At T294 start, C7 = 21 in the live repo, decomposable as T290-context 9 + T290-battery-spec 8 + T288-context 2 + T267-key-agreement 1 + T267-context 1 → 10 genuine, 11 context dumps, matching the brief's 2026-08-03 example exactly. During T294 the concurrent T293 worktree absorption (uncommitted CLAIMS.md + rejections.json changes, not mine) brought that count to 0; T294's own three proposed rows now measure C7=3, at/below threshold. (b) CODE.STANDING-C3-DEAD: the pre-existing STANDING-REEVIDENCE trigger CANNOT fire — cmdStanding looks for marker 'C3: ' (main.zig:4140) but claimlint never prints it (grep over full output finds nothing); c3_debt is always 0, and the condition 'c3_debt > c3_prior and c3_prior > 0' can never hold. (c) CODE.STANDING-STATE-FRAGILE: _standing priors persist only until the next kanban write — parseStateJson skips all '_'-prefixed keys (main.zig:581) and writeState re-serializes only task keys, so persistStandingState's textual insert is dropped by any add/claim/done; today's tasks.json has no _standing even though the Orchestrator saw fired triggers with 'was 0' priors. STANDING-ABSORB is unaffected (absolute trigger).

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH: exact C7 values at the three manual registrations (T279/T288/T293) — no historical claimlint snapshots in git, so the threshold rationale cites only the one fully decomposable observation (2026-08-03) plus the noise-band argument; I did not assert anything about those runs' counts.

WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON: (1) the C3-dead trigger (b above) — fixing it would touch a neighbouring trigger, which the brief says is the Orchestrator's call; reported as a row instead. (2) The _standing fragility (c above) — same reasoning. (3) The live repo's C7 fell from 21 to 3 during my session via T293's concurrent worktree absorption — I deliberately never ran `managent standing` against the live repo, because doing so would also auto-register the fired CONSOLIDATE/HOLISTIC-AUDIT triggers against the brief's explicit instruction, and because the live trigger state is the Orchestrator's surface to invoke.

ASSUMED WITHOUT CHECKING: that bin/weizigo-claimlint's summary line format ('C7 unabsorbed findings: N (FAILS)') is stable — it is the hook's own parse target class and claimlint is its single implementation; my parser takes leading digits so a suffix change cannot poison it.
